sentences.en: WOMAN: Hi Coleman, how are you?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 嗨，科尔曼，你好吗？

sentences.en: COLEMAN: Good, thanks.
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 很好，谢谢。

sentences.en: WOMAN: I wanted to have a chat with you because our friend Josh told me that you've joined a guitar group and it sounds interesting.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 我想找你聊聊，因为我们的朋友乔什告诉我，你加入了一个吉他小组，听起来很有意思。

sentences.en: I'd really like to learn myself.
sentences.zh: 我自己真的很想学。

sentences.en: COLEMAN: Why don't you come along?
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 你何不一起来呢？

sentences.en: I'm sure there's room for another person.
sentences.zh: 我肯定还有另一个名额。

sentences.en: WOMAN: Really?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 真的吗？

sentences.en: So - who runs the classes?
sentences.zh: 那么——谁负责授课？

sentences.en: COLEMAN: He's called 'coordinator' - his name's Gary Mathieson.
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 他被称为‘协调员’，名字叫加里·马西森。

sentences.en: WOMAN: Let me note that down.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 让我记下来。

sentences.en: Gary. . . .
sentences.zh: 加里……

sentences.en: How do you spell his surname?
sentences.zh: 他的姓氏怎么拼？

sentences.en: COLEMAN: It's M-A-T-H-I-E-S-O-N.
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 是 M-A-T-H-I-E-S-O-N。

sentences.en: WOMAN: Right, thanks.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 好的，谢谢。

sentences.en: Audioscripts
sentences.zh: 听力原文

sentences.en: COLEMAN: He's retired, actually, but he's a really nice guy and he used to play in a lot of bands.
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 他其实已经退休了，但人特别好，以前还在很多乐队里演奏过。

sentences.en: WOMAN: Thanks.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 谢谢。

sentences.en: So how long have you been going?
sentences.zh: 那你参加多久了？

sentences.en: COLEMAN: About a month now.
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 大概一个月了。

sentences.en: WOMAN: And could you play anything before you started?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 那你开始之前会弹任何曲子吗？

sentences.en: COLEMAN: knew a few chords, but that's all.
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 只懂几个和弦，仅此而已。

sentences.en: WOMAN: I'm sure everyone will be better than me.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 我肯定比所有人都差。

sentences.en: COLEMAN: That's what I thought, too.
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 我当初也是这么想的。

sentences.en: When I first spoke to Gary on the phone, he said it was a class for beginners, but I was still worried that everyone would be better than me, but we were all equally hopeless!
sentences.zh: 我第一次在电话里跟加里交谈时，他说这是个面向初学者的课程，但我还是担心别人都比我强；结果我们所有人一样‘惨不忍睹’！

sentences.en: WOMAN: Oh, that's reassuring.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 哦，这倒让人安心了。

sentences.en: So where do you meet?
sentences.zh: 那你们在哪里见面？

sentences.en: COLEMAN: Well, when I joined the group, they were meeting in Gary's home, but as the group got bigger, he decided to book a room at the college in town.
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 我刚加入时，大家是在加里家里上课，但随着人数增多，他决定在镇上的学院里租一间教室。

sentences.en: I prefer going there.
sentences.zh: 我更喜欢去那里上课。

sentences.en: WOMAN: know that place.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 我知道那个地方。

sentences.en: I used to go to tap dancing classes there when I was at secondary school.
sentences.zh: 我上中学时还在那儿上过踢踏舞课。

sentences.en: I haven't been since, though and can't remember what road it's in . . . is it Lock Street?
sentences.zh: 不过自那以后我就再没去过，也记不清它在哪条路上了……是洛克街吗？

sentences.en: COLEMAN: It's just beyond there at the bottom of New Street near the city roundabout.
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 就在洛克街再往前一点，新街尽头、靠近城市环岛的地方。

sentences.en: WOMAN: Yes, of course.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 啊，对，当然。

sentences.en: COLEMAN: The guitar club S on the first floor in Room T347.
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 吉他俱乐部在一层的T347教室。

sentences.en: WOMAN: Right.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 明白了。

sentences.en: And when do you meet?
sentences.zh: 那你们什么时候见面？

sentences.en: Is it at the weekend?
sentences.zh: 是在周末吗？

sentences.en: COLEMAN: We meet on Thursdays.
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 我们每周四见面。

sentences.en: It used to be 10.30 and that suited me well, but now we meet at 11.
sentences.zh: 以前是上午10:30，时间很适合我，但现在改到11点上课了。

sentences.en: The class that's in there before us asked if they could have the room for another 30 minutes.
sentences.zh: 在我们之前使用那间教室的班级，请求把使用时间延长30分钟。

sentences.en: WOMAN: Oh, see.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 哦，明白了。

sentences.en: Well, I'd love to come, but I don't have a guitar.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我很想去，但我没有吉他。

sentences.en: COLEMAN: Well, you can always buy a second-hand one.
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 哦，你随时可以买一把二手的。

sentences.en: There's a website called 'The perfect instrument' that sells all kinds of guitars, violins and so on.
sentences.zh: 有个叫‘完美乐器’的网站，出售各种吉他、小提琴等等。

sentences.en: I'm sure you'll find something there.
sentences.zh: 我相信你一定能在那里找到合适的。

sentences.en: WOMAN: So what's a typical lesson like with Gary?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 那么，加里老师的典型课程是什么样的呢？

sentences.en: COLEMAN: Well, he always starts by getting us to tune our guitars.
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 呃，他总是先让我们给吉他调音。

sentences.en: That takes about five minutes.
sentences.zh: 这大约需要五分钟。

sentences.en: WOMAN: Uhuh.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 嗯。

sentences.en: COLEMAN: Some people have an app they use, but others do it by ear.
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 有些人用手机应用程序来调音，但其他人则靠耳朵听音调准。

sentences.en: Gary goes round and helps them.
sentences.zh: 加里会走过来帮大家调音。

sentences.en: And while he's doing that, he tells us what he's going to do during the lesson.
sentences.zh: 而他在帮忙调音的同时，也会告诉我们这节课将要学习的内容。

sentences.en: WOMAN: Right.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 明白了。

sentences.en: COLEMAN: First, we usually spend about ten minutes doing some strumming.
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 首先，我们通常花大约十分钟练习拨弦。

sentences.en: WOMAN: So is that using .. what are they called plectrums?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 所以是用……它们叫什么来着？拨片吗？

sentences.en: COLEMAN: No - we just use our thumbs.
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 不——我们只用拇指。

sentences.en: WOMAN: Much easier.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 这样简单多了。

sentences.en: COLEMAN: Gary reminds us where to put our fingers for each chord and then we play them together.
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 加里会提醒我们每个和弦的手指该放在哪里，然后我们一起弹奏。

sentences.en: Sometimes we all just start laughing because we're so bad at keeping time, so Gary starts clapping to help us.
sentences.zh: 有时我们都会忍不住大笑起来，因为我们实在太难保持节奏一致了，于是加里就打拍子来帮我们。

sentences.en: WOMAN: Do you learn to play any songs?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 你们会学弹歌曲吗？

sentences.en: COLEMAN: Yes - we - do at least one song with words and chords.
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 是的——我们至少会学一首带歌词和和弦的歌曲。

sentences.en: I mean that's harder than you think.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这可比你想象中难得多。

sentences.en: WOMAN: Oh, I'm sure it is!
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 哦，我确信确实如此！

sentences.en: COLEMAN: That part of the lesson takes about 15 minutes.
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 这部分课程大约持续十五分钟。

sentences.en: He often brings a recording of a the song and plays it to us first.
sentences.zh: 他常常会带来一首歌的录音，先放给我们听。

sentences.en: Then he hands out the song and if there's a new chord in it, we practise that before we play it together - but really slowly.
sentences.zh: 接着他分发乐谱；如果其中包含新和弦，我们会先单独练习这个和弦，然后再一起演奏——但速度非常慢。

sentences.en: WOMAN: Do you do any finger picking?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 你们会练习指弹吗？

sentences.en: COLEMAN: That's the last ten minutes of the lesson, when we pick out the individual notes from a tune he's made up.
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 这是课程最后十分钟的内容，我们从他编的一段曲子里逐个弹出单音。

sentences.en: It's always quite simple.
sentences.zh: 曲子总是相当简单。

sentences.en: WOMAN: That must be hard, though.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 尽管如此，那一定很难吧。

sentences.en: COLEMAN: It is, but people like it because they can really concentrate and if we're all playing well, it sounds quite impressive.
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 的确很难，但大家很喜欢，因为可以全神贯注；而且如果我们都能弹得不错，整体效果听起来还挺震撼的。

sentences.en: The only trouble is that he sometimes gets us to play one at a time you know, alone.
sentences.zh: 唯一的麻烦是，他有时会让我们一个一个地单独演奏。

sentences.en: WOMAN: That's scary.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 那真吓人。

sentences.en: COLEMAN: It is, but I've got used to it now.
sentences.zh: COLEMAN: 确实如此，不过我现在已经习惯了。

sentences.en: At the end he spends about five minutes telling us what to practise for the following week.
sentences.zh: 课末，他会花大约五分钟告诉我们下周需要练习的内容。

sentences.en: WOMAN: Well, thanks Coleman.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 好的，谢谢您，科尔曼。

sentences.en: I'll go and have a look at that website, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想我会去那个网站看看。
